title: Finite etale direct image and ordinary adic cohomology
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $X,Y$ be noetherian finite-dimensional schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite etale morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $(F_n)_{n\geq1}$ be a compatible system of finite locally constant finite free $A_n$-module sheaves on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$, with specified transition isomorphisms $F_{n+1}\otimes_{A_{n+1}}A_n\cong F_n$. Let $F_{\mathcal O_E}$ be its derived-complete integral realization [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], let $F_E$ be its rationalization, and let $F_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$ be its scalar extension in the common-finite-stage adic category [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. Write $F_\Lambda$ for any of these realizations, including $F_{A_n}=F_n$. Ordinary cohomology here means derived global sections in these coefficient categories, not cohomology of discrete non-torsion sheaves on the small etale site.

The systems $(f_*F_n)_n$ are compatible finite locally constant finite free systems. Their integral, rational and algebraically closed coefficient realizations, denoted $f_*F_\Lambda$, agree with $Rf_*F_\Lambda$ and are concentrated in sheaf degree zero. The canonical comparison is an isomorphism
$$
R\Gamma(X,f_*F_\Lambda)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(Y,F_\Lambda),\qquad
H^i(X,f_*F_\Lambda)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(Y,F_\Lambda)\quad(i\geq0).
$$
These comparisons are natural in the coefficient system, commute with the finite quotient transitions and scalar extension, and intertwine an automorphism $h:Y\to Y$ over $X$ acting by pullback on $F_\Lambda$ with its induced action on $f_*F_\Lambda$.

For every morphism $u:X'\to X$ with $X'$ noetherian and finite-dimensional and with $\ell$ invertible on $X'$, put $Y'=Y\times_X X'$, with projections $v:Y'\to Y$ and $f':Y'\to X'$. The canonical exchange $u^*f_*F_\Lambda\to f'_*v^*F_\Lambda$ is an isomorphism at all the displayed coefficient stages. It commutes with endomorphisms of the coefficient systems, hence with their character idempotents.

source.place: First displayed finite-pushforward cohomology comparison; adic coefficient extension of the finite torsion assertion, based at finite level on Stacks Tag 03QP, etale-cohomology-proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero (literature/stacks-project/etale-cohomology.tex).

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $G_n=f_{\mathrm{et},*}F_n$. Finite direct image is exact by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact], and [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] gives its finite fibre product. More precisely, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split] supplies an etale covering $U\to X$ on which $Y_U=\coprod_{j\in J}U$, with $J$ finite. By [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange], $G_n|_U=\prod_{j\in J}F_{n,j}$. Refining $U$ to trivialize the finitely many $F_{n,j}$ shows that $G_n$ is locally constant finite free; the rank may vary between components, and an empty fibre gives rank zero. A finite product of modules is their direct sum, and tensor distributes over that finite sum. Therefore the given maps induce $G_{n+1}\otimes_{A_{n+1}}A_n\cong G_n$: additivity alone is not being used to commute tensor with pushforward. The identifications are canonical, since their maps are induced by the quotient maps and the finite-exchange maps.

For either normalized system $M_\bullet=F_\bullet$ on $Y$ or $G_\bullet$ on $X$, write $N_n=\nu^*M_n$ on the pro-etale site and $N=\lim_nN_n$. The transition is a sheaf epimorphism: its cokernel is zero because it is the quotient $M_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow M_{n+1}/\varpi^nM_{n+1}=M_n$, and $\nu^*$ is exact by [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]. Repleteness is [det-pe-replete-epimorphism], and [det-pe-continuous-cohomology-limit] gives $N[0]\simeq R\lim_nN_n$. This is a sheaf inverse-limit assertion, without any passage of $R\lim$ through geometric stalks. It also holds with completed $A$-module coefficients: the Roos map on module products has the same underlying abelian map, and module products are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Thus both realizations have sheaf amplitude $[0,0]$.

source.place: Propositions 3.1.9 and 3.1.10; locally weakly contractible pro-etale topoi, Proposition 4.2.8

proof.text:
The reductions of this actual limit are the specified finite sheaves, including their quotient maps. To check this without adding separatedness to the item, restrict to any affine open $W$ of $X$ or $Y$. It is Noetherian and separated, so [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] applies to $M_ ullet|_W$: its inverse equivalence is precisely $N|_W=\lim_n
u_W^*(M_n|_W)$, and its reductions are $M_n|_W$. It also makes $N|_W$ pro-etale locally finite free over the completed coefficient sheaf. On a free chart, tensor with $A_n$ is a finite direct sum of tensor with the unit, so ordinary and derived reduction agree. Restriction to slice sites is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]; under [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] it is sectionwise restriction, hence commutes with the products and kernels computing limits. These local reduction isomorphisms are the maps induced by the same projections $N	o N_n$, so agree on overlaps. Their kernels and cokernels vanish on the affine cover, hence vanish globally. Consequently $N\otimes^L A_n\cong
u^*M_n$, coherently in $n$. Step 2 now proves derived completeness; the reductions are constructible in the fixed interval $[0,0]$. In particular, for $K=F_A$ we have the required specified witnesses $K\otimes^LA_n\cong
u_Y^*F_n$, not an identification between discrete integral etale sheaves and completed ones.

proof.text: Finite $f$ is affine and in particular quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] with the discrete ring $A_n$ and the degree-zero etale complex $F_n$. Together with Step 1 it gives $Rf_{\mathrm{proet},*,A_n}\nu_Y^*F_n\cong\nu_X^*G_n$ in degree zero. The comparison intertwines units, counits and pullback composition. Hence its mate identifies the pro-etale finite-level exchange with the etale exchange of [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange]: both are the unit, the pullback-square isomorphism and the counit in that order. This use of mate pasting is [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. In particular the pro-etale exchange is invertible for every indicated $u$. All maps respect the quotient transitions, since those are morphisms of the coefficient systems and the comparison is natural.

source.place: Tag 09A6, direct-image comparison for qcqs morphisms; etale-cohomology.tex, Tag 0959

proof.text: By [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison] and Step 3, ordinary completed-ring derived direct image has the canonical comparison $Rf_{*,A}K\cong R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n Rf_{*,A_n}(\nu_Y^*F_n)$. Its projection at $n$ is the direct image of the reduction map, followed by coefficient restriction. Step 4 identifies this tower, with its actual quotient transitions, with $(\nu_X^*G_n)_n$. Steps 2 and 3 identify its derived limit with the degree-zero integral realization of $G_\bullet$. Thus $Rf_{*,A}K=f_*F_A$ with the required sheaf amplitude. In addition [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] identifies the canonical projection-formula reduction map $(Rf_{*,A}K)\otimes^LA_n\to Rf_{*,A_n}(K\otimes^LA_n)$ as an isomorphism, coherently for all quotients. These are the reduction comparisons used below. This proves preservation of the constructible category for this $f$ and this system; no preservation theorem for an arbitrary structure morphism is invoked. The completed ring here is $R_W=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$ of sheafified constant sheaves, as in the item's integral category, while Steps 3, 6 and 7 use the ring $A_W$ of the adic coefficient datum. Since $\mathcal O_E$ is Noetherian and every $A_n$ is finite, the final clause of [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] gives $(A_n)_W=(P_n)_W$ and $R_W=A_W$. So the two module derived categories coincide. By Steps 2–3, $F_A$ is derived complete, has constructible reductions of amplitude $[0,0]$ and has compatible etale-origin witnesses. It therefore lies in both integral categories, and the same holds for $f_*F_A$.

source.place: Tag 099N (lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case); sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), with the cited completed-coefficient comparisons

proof.text: Consider the actual integral exchange $\alpha:L u^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K\to Rf'_*L v^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$. By [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction] its source reduces to $u_n^*((Rf_*K)_n)$, and its target reduces, using Step 5 for the finite etale $f'$, to $Rf'_{*,A_n}v_n^*K_n$. The equality of this specified ambient mate with the completed exchange assembled from the finite-level transformations is the last clause of [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange]. In particular, under these reduction comparisons the diagram has top arrow $\alpha\otimes^LA_n$ and bottom arrow the finite-level exchange of Step 4; the vertical arrows are exactly the projection-induced comparisons, and the diagram commutes. The same cited clause identifies the assembled arrow with $R\lim$ of those exchanges under the canonical source and target limit comparisons; it is not inferred from equality of evaluated arrows. Both endpoints are derived complete by [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction, prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. The bottom arrow for $n=1$ is invertible, so [sk-lem-pe-derived-nakayama] proves that $\alpha$ itself is invertible. Here Nakayama detects invertibility, not equality of morphisms. Step 3 identifies the completed pullback of these lisse systems with the realization of their pulled-back finite levels, so this is exactly the exchange asserted in the item.

source.place: Tag 099N, completed pullback and direct image; canonical mate/reduction compatibility as stated in lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange; derived Nakayama

proof.text: Rationalize the integral identifications by [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]; all the operations and maps are $A$-linear, and on morphisms the descended map is $a\otimes c\mapsto T(a)c$. Thus the isomorphisms and their commutative diagrams remain isomorphisms and commutative diagrams at $E$. For $E\subset L$, [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] identifies scalar extension of direct image and completed pullback, and explicitly identifies scalar extension of the canonical exchange with the canonical $L$-exchange. The restrictions are legitimate: Steps 1–6, now for $\mathcal O_L$, show constructibility and amplitude $[0,0]$ for the objects involved. The finite-level finite-product description also shows that coefficient extension of $G_\bullet$ is the pushforward of the coefficient extension of $F_\bullet$. The associators and successive-extension equations in that proposition, with [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], give the claimed common-finite-stage $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ identifications. Each is represented by a lisse degree-zero object at a finite stage, giving the stated degree-zero assertion at the rational and common stages.

source.place: First displayed finite-pushforward comparison, interpreted at integral, rational and common finite coefficient stages

proof.text: For finite coefficients use the ringed etale topoi, and for integral coefficients the completed-ring pro-etale topoi. Let $a_X$ be the morphism from the relevant topos of $X$ to the topos of sets equipped with the constant ring $\Lambda$; the structural ring map is the constant-section map $\Lambda\to\Gamma(X,R_X)$. Its direct image on modules is precisely $\Gamma(X,-)$ valued in all $\Lambda$-modules. The composite $a_Xf$ is $a_Y$, with the same coefficient action. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to these two ringed-topos morphisms and invert its $\kappa$ to obtain $R\Gamma(X,Rf_*F_\Lambda)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(Y,F_\Lambda)$. Its normalization is the direct-image composition map on K-injective resolutions, hence it is the canonical section comparison. Substitute Steps 1 and 5 and take $H^i$. All categories here are the ambient unbounded module derived categories, so no bounded-constructible cohomology assertion at a base scheme is needed.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; apply to the ringed topos of a point, not to Spec Z[1/ell]

proof.text: The rational global-sections functor on an integral representative $M$ is the $A$-linear ambient functor of Step 8 followed by $-\otimes_A E$ on module complexes. It descends to raw rationalization by the explicit rule $a\otimes c\mapsto R\Gamma(a)\otimes c$; this uses the Hom formula of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Therefore tensoring the canonical integral comparison of Step 8 with $E$ is the canonical rational comparison and is an isomorphism. This construction takes values in the whole $D(E)$, with no finite-dimensional or bounded-output requirement. For a further finite stage $L$, [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] gives a finite free coefficient extension of rank $[L:E]$. After a coefficient basis is chosen, commutation with ambient derived sections is the identity on a finite direct sum of copies of $R\Gamma(M)$; the resulting map is the canonical tensor-to-sections map, so is independent of that basis. Rationalizing gives the $E\subset L$ section comparison. The associators on the full $D(E)$ are [lem-weil-derived-field-scalar-extension-tower]. Hence $R\Gamma((E,M))=R\Gamma_E(M)\otimes_E\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ is well defined for the common-stage category, and the same canonical comparison is an isomorphism there. Taking $H^i$ proves the remaining cohomology assertions.

source.place: Propositions 6.8.4 and 6.8.14: lisse and constructible rational realization; raw localization and full module-valued derived sections as above

proof.text: All finite-level maps are natural in $F_n$ and in maps of coefficient systems. The projection normalizations in Steps 3–6 and the scalar associators in Steps 7–9 retain that naturality and its quotient-transition compatibilities. For an automorphism $h$ over $X$, pull back the system along $h$; the equality $fh=f$ identifies its pushforward with that of the original system. The normalized composition and its compatibility with adjunctions in [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] make the section comparison intertwine this pullback with the induced pushforward action. If an action on the same coefficient system is specified, insert its map $h^*F\to F$; naturality yields the claimed intertwining on that system. Finally, for any coefficient endomorphism $e$ the naturality square for the exchange of Step 6 commutes, by [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange]; the scalar comparison in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] preserves it at later stages. Take $e$ to be each defined character idempotent. No character projector is asserted over a coefficient ring where its defining denominator is not invertible.
